headline_marked: NCP leader [[Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir sent to jail]] over Facebook posts
headline: NCP leader Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir sent to jail over Facebook posts
summary: The suspended joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party was arrested in Dhaka and produced before a Bogura court.
details: A Bogura court has sent Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, the recently suspended joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP), to jail. He faces charges for allegedly making derogatory remarks about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on social media.

Police arrested Tanvir at around 5:30 am in the Manipur area of Dhaka before producing him before the Bogura Sadar Cognisance Court. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mehedi Hasan passed the jail order at approximately 12:00 pm today.

The case was filed on August 2 by Maftun Ahmed Khan Rubel, president of the Bogura Sadar Upazila BNP unit. The lawsuit, filed under the Cyber Security Act 2026, accuses Tanvir of making defamatory Facebook posts targeting the prime minister.

According to the case statement, Tanvir allegedly posted derogatory content on July 29 regarding recent attacks in Sylhet. He is reported to have made another provocative post shortly after, repeating similar insinuations.
In response to the posts, the NCP's central executive committee relieved Tanvir of his position as joint member secretary on July 31 and issued him a show-cause notice.

headline_marked: Journalists rally as [[Bangladesh observes July Mass Uprising Day]]
headline: Journalists rally as Bangladesh observes July Mass Uprising Day
summary: Members of the BFUJ and DUJ held a colorful rally in Dhaka to mark the anniversary of the student-led uprising and demand justice for the martyrs.
details: The Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ) organized a colorful rally in Dhaka on Wednesday to mark the anniversary of the historic student-led uprising.
The rally began from the National Press Club premises, where participating journalists paid deep respect to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives during the July mass uprising.
Journalist leaders demanded a swift trial and exemplary punishment for those involved in the brutal killings that took place during the July events.
They warned that various conspiracies, both domestic and external, are being carried out to undermine the achievements and spirit of the July uprising.
Kader Gani Chowdhury emphasized that the journalist community must play a united role in ensuring full media freedom and maintaining a democratic environment in the country.
The day is being observed across the country to commemorate the fall of fascism and the victory of the students and the general public.
caption:
Journalists take to the streets to demand justice for the martyrs of the July Mass Uprising.

The Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ) organized a colorful rally in Dhaka on Wednesday to mark the anniversary of the historic student-led uprising.

details

The rally began from the National Press Club premises, where participating journalists paid deep respect to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives during the July mass uprising.

Journalist leaders demanded a swift trial and exemplary punishment for those involved in the brutal killings that took place during the July events.

They warned that various conspiracies, both domestic and external, are being carried out to undermine the achievements and spirit of the July uprising.

Kader Gani Chowdhury emphasized that the journalist community must play a united role in ensuring full media freedom and maintaining a democratic environment in the country.

The day is being observed across the country to commemorate the fall of fascism and the victory of the students and the general public.
